answers.solution:
SYMPTOM: killing a pytest run mid-suite (worker dispatch killed by a foreman, timeout --kill, ctrl-C) leaves a leaked live DuckBrain test namespace named auger-pytest-<session-tag>-<12hex> in BOTH the registry API scan and ~/duckbrain/namespaces/. The NEXT full-gate run then FAILS its leak audit: tests/test_auger.py::test_no_test_namespace_survives_the_suite asserts leftovers(CREATED) == {'api': [], 'disk': []} and names the dead session's namespace.

WHY: the suite invents a per-session tag (uuid4 hex[:8]) at conftest import time; every namespace it creates carries auger-pytest-<tag>-. The sanctioned cleanup helper tests/conftest.py::teardown_namespace REFUSES any name outside ITS OWN session tag (anti-footgun: it can never rmtree a real namespace), so a dead session's leak cannot be cleaned with the normal helper - it raises ValueError.

FIX (verified in repo auger, tick 2026-11-21): with the owning session confirmed DEAD (pgrep pytest, lock holder gone), perform the documented two-step teardown manually:
1. DELETE via the API - auger.delete_namespace(ns); 404 counts as gone (do NOT hand-delete a registry row some other process still owns).
2. Remove the disk half: rm -rf ~/duckbrain/namespaces/<ns> (only names carrying the auger-pytest- prefix).
3. Prove the audit function clean before re-running the gate: from tests.conftest import leftovers; leftovers() must return {'api': [], 'disk': []}.

NOTES: a LIVING sibling session's in-flight namespace is NOT a leak (the audit scopes to CREATED); historical auger-pytest-* rows from long-dead sessions may still sit in the API list - they do not trip the per-session audit, do not mass-delete them unasked. Also kill the orphaned `timeout --kill-after=30s 2400s ... pytest` wrapper, not just the pytest child.

- After manual two-step teardown of 2 leaked namespaces, leftovers() returned {'api': [], 'disk': []} and the next full guard passed

signatures.description: A pytest run killed mid-suite leaks its live-gate DuckBrain test namespace (api+disk) and the next gate's leak audit fails on the dead session's name; the suite's own teardown helper refuses cross-session names. DIAGNOSIS: read the audit failure for the leaked name; confirm the owning tag's session is dead (no pytest, lock free). FIX: API DELETE (404=ok) then rmtree ~/duckbrain/namespaces/<ns>, then assert leftovers() == empty. VERIFY: rerun the gate; leak audit must pass.
